utterances.text: Yes, General, can you answer the question? Or can you help us?

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Was that your personal experience or did you find that in the documents that you analysed?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: So, I didn't take part in this personally, but I read that or I saw that, rather, in the documents, thus I did not take part in these events.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: But did you cite it in your report, General?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure that I referred to this paragraph. I would need to check, I would need to look at it.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Thank you. I would just ask for the General to check so he can point me to the document which supports that statement.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Shall we continue in the meantime?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. But Mr. Nicholls suggested that the civilians in Mahala were the target of the action. That's why I asked. Can we tender this document, please?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we'll mark it for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As MFI D3902, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Are we going to conclude Mr. Keserovic's evidence or not? We have to continue next week now?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] We have to continue next week. Should we continue or should we finish for today?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Yes, we have seven minutes.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you. Can I now ask to see 65 ter -- actually, 1D30 in e-court. I'm sorry, 1D31, please. Page 6 in the Serbian. The cover page is the same but we would need to look at page 6 in the Serbian of 1D31.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: General, sir, did you see this is a book by two Muslim authors from Sanski Most. We looked at this before.

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have the opportunity to see this book.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] English page 2, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look, did you have the opportunity to see this book before?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I did have the opportunity. I did see it before.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Could you please look at the second paragraph, it's the second paragraph from the bottom in English. Could you please tell us in which villages and suburbs were these preparations formed, these armed preparations?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: These are Vrhpolje, Trnovo, Hrustovo, Sehovci, Kamengrad, and then of the city or the suburban areas, that would be Mahala and Muhici.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: And then it says that this made the preparations more difficult. Were the civilians in Mahala the target and do you know where they were transferred to during the fighting? Did you find in the documents where they were transferred to during the fighting?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were transferred, but I'm not quite sure to which neighbourhood or settlement they were transferred, but they were transferred.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you. Can you please link up -- actually, do you remember that ultimatum? What was it that the civilians were asked and what were these armed ones asked to do?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: The civilians were asked to respect law and order and not to contribute in any way to the growing problems of any kind and the armed ones were asked to surrender their weapons.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Could we look at the previous page in the Serbian, please, and I believe in the English as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Among these people who were preparing the rebellion and the fighting, can you find any names that we mentioned today or any names that you were asked about by Mr. Nicholls?

utterances.speaker: DRAGOMIR KESEROVIC [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I can see the name Faik Biscevic here.

utterances.speaker: MR. KARADZIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Can I tender this, please?

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: No objection to it being marked, but it appears to me to be partial translations of pages. I think at least the full pages should be translated, not just paragraphs. And I would want to look at it --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Robinson, if you could assist us. We dealt with this book before or not? I think I -- we saw this book before.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I believe that we did admit an excerpt from the same book, where it says that they -- that Serbs attacked only when they decided to move against the Serbs, from Hrustovo, from these villages, something like that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I don't think we admitted it. So ... Yes, in light of the witness's evidence and response from the Prosecution, we'll mark for identification this page -- the pages shown to the witness. Yes, Mr. Nicholls.

utterances.speaker: MR. NICHOLLS
utterances.text: Your Honours, Mr. Reid tells me at least part of this was admitted as D1677.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you. D1677. Then we will add these pages to that exhibit, but I -- with the caveat that there should be full translation. Given the time, shall we adjourn for today, Mr. Karadzic?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Mr. Keserovic, do you have any difficulty staying over the weekend until Monday to conclude your evidence?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have no choice.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Thank you for your kind understanding. Yes, Mr. Robinson -- ah, we have another witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. ROBINSON
utterances.text: Yes, but that witness has been allotted two hours of cross-examination, so I think General Keserovic will start about 12.00 on Monday and hopefully we should complete his evidence on Monday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: Very well. Yes, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: MR. TIEGER
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. President. In connection with our expedited response to the motion for adjournment, we would be greatly assisted by an extension of the word limit of approximately 800 words. I communicated to Mr. Robinson this request and he has no objection.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: It is granted, Mr. Tieger.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: I was told that the pages shown to the witness today were already marked for identification.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: As part of Exhibit D1677, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: The hearing is adjourned.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE KWON
utterances.text: to be reconvened on Monday, the 29th day of July, 2013, at 9.00 a.m.
